author: Gamerforlfe
title: Game is getting worse
content:
Township is becoming less and less enjoyable, and the recent changes are making it incredibly difficult to justify continuing to play.

The Match-3 game is a perfect example. Somehow, the game gets harder when you actually have power-ups and noticeably easier when you run out of them. What is the point of earning power-ups if having them seems to make the levels more difficult? It feels completely backwards.

On top of that, the levels have become ridiculously difficult. There is a difference between making a game challenging and making it frustrating enough that players feel forced to use power-ups or spend in-game currency just to progress. At this point, it feels like the difficulty is being designed around getting players to spend money rather than giving them an enjoyable challenge.

And then there’s Frozen Fortune, which is arguably even worse. It doesn’t seem to matter whether I’m spinning at x1, x5, or x10. I consistently can’t seem to get spins above 150. So what exactly is the point of earning more moves if the game is going to keep limiting your progress anyway? It makes the entire event feel predetermined rather than something where strategy or luck actually matters.

I’ve played Township because it was fun. That is the part that seems to be getting lost. Everything is becoming more expensive, progression is becoming more frustrating, and more and more of the game feels designed around convincing players to spend money.

I’m not against spending money on a game I enjoy. I’m against feeling like I have to spend money to enjoy the game at all.

The developers need to seriously reconsider the direction they’re taking. Players shouldn’t have to constantly fight the game itself just to have fun.

Township doesn’t need more ways to monetize the player. It needs to become fun again.

author: HiroshiMishima
title: Fun But Flawed
content:
All the potential in Township is overshadowed by the insane greed which can be most blatantly seen in the obnoxious match 3 games. So many of them boil down to getting incredibly lucky, some are downright designed to be basically impossible without paying for boosters like the weight or drill.

Unfortunately, you can't simply ignore the match 3 because they are constantly shoving it in your face. All events revolve around it, which is strange considering the seeming main presence of the farm town you're building. And talk about insulting, the little tune that plays - even when the music is off - when you fail or give up on a match 3 feels like rubbing salt in the wound.

I like the farming stuff, building the town is fun. Once again, though, it's sullied by the need to harass the player to pay money. The barn has an excruciatingly small capacity and it takes a long time to upgrade it even once unless you get lucky with the trains. Then you have multiple requests from different directions for time based resources, so it quickly becomes tedious and tiresome. You can't build things without stuff like bricks or nails, so you need to do the trains, but then you have all the plane and helicopter requests for items and there is no way to keep up with it all.

I enjoyed the game a lot in the beginning, but now I'm over 100 match 3 stages in and almost to level 19 on the farm and it's just not fun anymore. I don't know how people can keep playing but they're probably spending money...

author: Dinglehopper69
title: DO NOT USE REAL MONEY IN GAME
content:
First off, the game is NOTHING like you might see in ads. It is in fact free to play, but like any grow games you need to do a bunch of side quests. 

This is where it’s immediately obvious the algorithms are working hard against you. Every single type or weekly quest, team challenge, etc is directly tied into the puzzle games. You really can’t progress without doing them. 

This is where you might get hooked. The more/faster you play the puzzles the faster it gets harder (as expected) but then you’ll notice pieces just conveniently do not drop the way it’s supposed to, tools aren’t working the way it should, etc. It’ll let you get close to completion on one category and the second you spend actual money on the game, boom. You’re cooked. 

I actually placed a refund request with Apple and it was refunded almost immediately. That alone seemed like an admission of guilt on the developers part.

You’re able to talk to your fellow teammates once you join a team. This is about the only straight forward part of the game. I’d say more than half of the members agree that it’s rigged. The other half consists of rotating members who ultimately quit. Thankfully you are able to help (in terms of crop/product) but you’re on your own with the puzzle aspect.

It’s clear that he top players are paying loads of money into the game … weekly/daily. Some have even admitted to such. It’s a shame. Despite being nothing like the advertising, the game has potential if not for its unethical development.
